messages.content: You are a skeptical ICLR reviewer. Reject renaming known failures; return only valid JSON.

{"request": "Return JSON only with keys verdict (RUN_ONE or REJECT_ALL), novelty_score_0_to_10, one_sentence_claim, carrier, exact_legal_operation, mechanism_observable, short_gate, defense, core_tasks, overlap_risks, rationale. We need a genuinely broad world-model security claim after the following failures. TD-MPC2 legal temporal cascade only harmed fixed cheetah-run->walker-run and failed source-seed/task-family/independent-carrier replication. MBRL-Lib rank/sampler coupling failed stronger tasks. A proposed cross-carrier provenance-shadowing attack on native MBRL-Lib Pusher was tested: legal boundary prefixes increased rollout RMSE 0.716->1.213 but also increased ensemble disagreement 0.00496->0.00798 and did not reduce native CEM return. A source-update ensemble-synchronization variant raised residual correlation .766->.926 only at 20 updates while one-step RMSE rose .259->.384; at 5 updates correlation only .800 and RMSE .293; boundary and shuffled controls were similar. Reject ordinary forgetting, negative transfer, OOD/uncertainty collapse, rollout compounding, sampler coupling, prompt injection, backdoors, goal leakage, and changed planners. Consider available carriers: (a) MBRL-Lib native ensemble/CEM on CartPole, Pusher, Reacher3D, HalfCheetah; (b) WorldAgen LIBERO checkpoint with images/states/actions and native model forward, but weak closed-loop baseline; (c) WorldEvolver/ScienceWorld structured episodic+semantic world model and native LLM agent; (d) DiscoveryWorld. We specifically want an action-discriminative or evidence-provenance mechanism: factual one-step and actor/on-policy behavior remain matched, but unexecuted action contrasts or corrective observations are selectively misinterpreted. The operation must use only legal simulator actions and true observations/rewards, be implementable in <=2 minutes, and have a mechanism metric plus a clean repair. If no candidate can plausibly reach novelty 7-7.5 and a multi-task paper, return REJECT_ALL."}

  "rationale": "Every proposed direction relies on the premise that an attacker can feed legal trajectories during model fitting or memory ingestion such that on-policy states retain low RMSE while off-policy/counterfactual action evaluations are distorted without triggering ensemble disagreement. In continuous MBRL (e.g., MBRL-Lib PETS/CEM), any legal data update that alters the model's derivative with respect to action space inevitably degrades rollout fidelity or collapses calibration unless constrained by the true dynamics manifold; empirical results provided already show this (RMSE increases from 0.716 to 1.213 and ensemble disagreement rises concurrently). In structured/LLM carriers (LIBERO, ScienceWorld), 'evidence-provenance' distortion reduces cleanly to context contamination, retrieval recency bias, or standard goal/belief overwrite. The requirement that this does not constitute ordinary negative transfer, distribution shift, or capacity saturation cannot be satisfied by standard neural networks trained on legal data points. Without an artificial backdoor trigger or non-standard objective, this behavior is the textbook definition of training-induced gradient interference. No proposal achieves the required novelty threshold of 7.0+ for ICLR."
